items.title: The enforcement asymmetry I12 created: the reference checker enforces the decisions, the independent implementation's checker does not
items.hypothesis: An IND re-run against v1.3.0 (adopting an I12-equivalent check in its own checker) would restore symmetry: both implementations enforcing, not merely following, the registered decisions.
items.discriminatingTest: The independent implementation's own inversion ablations caught by its own I12-equivalent at 22,440 / 38,760, matching the reference-side measurements it already published.
items.whyItMatters: Grounded in this run's own claim discipline: 'the independent implementation -- whose checker is its own -- has not run against v1.3.0.' Until then, cross-implementation agreement is agreement of two evaluators but enforcement exists on one side only. Optional, owner's commission, packaging rules LEAK-101/LEAK-102 binding.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Strengthens (or is a precondition some owners would set for) the verified-independent promotion.
items.cost: one commission; the implementer's checker change is small (its ablations already exist)

items.title: Retire or version-guard the stale whole-document reproduction check (VER-101)
items.hypothesis: A version-aware comparator (or an explicit retirement note in the v1.0.0 REPRODUCE.md pointing at the versioned documents) removes the one known-stale verification path left by I12's permanent presence in the checker.
items.discriminatingTest: A fresh reproduction of any registration passes its documented comparison without consulting tribal knowledge.
items.whyItMatters: VER-101, recorded by this run: the checker now carries I12 and baseline reports carry two new fields, so REPRODUCE.md's original one-liner fails against fresh reproductions for reasons that are not defects. A stale check that fails honestly is better than one that passes wrongly, but both erode trust in checks.
items.cost: documentation plus ~20 lines, but note the v1.0.0 REPRODUCE.md is a registered artifact -- the fix is a pointer file or the versioned documents, not an edit
